scenes.text: Shine a UV light on a platypus, and its fur glows blue green.
Scientists only found this out in twenty twenty.
They tested museum platypus specimens in Chicago and Nebraska under ultraviolet light.
In normal light, the fur looks plain brown.
But under UV, it gives off an eerie blue green glow.
Males and females glowed in a similar way, so it probably isn't about attracting mates.
Nobody knows yet what the glow is for.
Before that, the only glowing mammals known were opossums and flying squirrels, which glow pink.
And the platypus was already one of the weirdest animals alive.
It's a mammal that lays eggs.
Males have venomous spurs on the inside of their ankles.
Mothers don't feed through nipples; milk seeps out of pores on their belly.
Underwater, they don't rely much on sight, and their bill can sense tiny electric signals.
Their thick fur keeps them warm in cold water.
They hunt mostly at night in the rivers of eastern Australia.
Which animal do you think glows next?

title: Platypuses glow under UV light ✨
caption: A 2020 study in Mammalia found platypus fur glows blue-green under ultraviolet light. Nobody knows why yet.
